newsitem.title: USA: Dollar ends week of breathtaking gains sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Dollar ends week of breathtaking gains sharply higher.

text.p: Swept up by a powerful wave of bullish momentum and more good news on the U.S. economy, the dollar surged Friday to its highest level against the Swiss franc in four years and rose against the German mark for a fifth consecutive session.
The dollar also culminated a week of breathtaking gains with a jump to a two-month high against the Japanese yen, helped by a substantial fall in the yen against the mark.
Dealers said recent dollar strength against the mark was showing clear signs of filtering through to broad dollar gains against other major currencies, suggesting the rally is far from over.
"I think the dollar is still in a sharp uptrend against the mark with no downward correction in sight," said Russell LaScala, chief dealer at Citibank.
"And this move against the Swiss franc suggests we've opened the door for a broader catch-up" against other currencies, he added.
The dollar set another six-year high against the mark, rising to an intraday peak of 1.8403 and ending at 1.8378 marks, up from 1.8348 Thursday.

It also pushed up to a top of 0.8262 Swiss francs -- its highest level since August 1993 -- before settling at 1.5160 against 1.5065. Against the yen, the dollar rose as high as 116.99 and ended at 116.95 vs. 116.05 Thursday.

The dollar found support from a Commerce Department report that showed U.S. orders for durable goods, or big-ticket items such as cars and appliances, rose by 2.3 percent in June, much higher than economists had expected.
It also benefited indirectly from a rebound in the mark against the currencies of its European neighbours and against the yen.
Remarks from members of Germany's central bank helped stabilise the mark and limit its weakness against the dollar, dealers said.

Bundesbank Vice President Johann Wilhelm Gaddum was quoted in a European weekly newspaper Friday as saying the dollar was slightly overvalued against the mark, but that mark weakness was not sparking inflationary pressures in Germany.

Meanwhile, Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen told a German daily that central bank policy-makers were "driving carefully" in the current exchange rate environment, suggesting they could manipulate interest rates to bolster the mark if it fell too far.
"The Bundesbank has definitely added an element of caution to the market," said Stephen Flanagan, vice president of corporate foreign exchange at Credit Agricole Indosuez.
But the dollar's advance in the face of the Bundesbank remarks showed the momentum of the current rally and the potential for further gains, traders said.
"We are ending at the highest weekly closing levels of the year against virtually all the major European currencies, except sterling," said Flanagan.
The British pound closed at $1.6640, down from $1.6745 on Thursday. The dollar climbed to Canadian $1.3847 from C$1.3818.
